```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day constraint favors B's channel. B sells through the Shopify App Store, a self-serve marketplace with built-in merchant discovery and no outbound sales. A's own seed company reports about 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal, which alone exceeds the 90-day window.",
    "A one-person operator with AI agents can plausibly run B's acquisition paths: App Store ads at about $6 CPC, and SEO comparison content at $300–$1,500 per article. A's sourced alternatives are founder office visits, which AI agents don't obviously replace, or a $3,475–$4,500 PestWorld booth that is already sold out for 2026.",
    "B's product scope is narrow and well-defined: a checkout survey widget, an exit-intent popup, a dashboard, and Klaviyo/Flow integrations. That makes a 6-week build credible. Its regulatory burden (GDPR/CCPA DPA) is a standard one-time review, while A carries wage-law and 1099 commission exposure for an unstaffed operator.",
    "B's low price points ($25–$49/mo) and free-tier competition hurt long-term revenue, but they lower the barrier to a first paying customer. Self-serve SMB merchants can convert without a procurement or trust cycle.",
    "Both ideas face saturated competition (6+ direct competitors each), so competition does not separate them. The deciding factor is time-to-first-sale fit, and there B is clearly stronger."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence doesn't match the stated payer. The brief says the owner or sales-ops manager pays, yet both demand quotes come from the rep side. One is a tech's complaint on a low-reliability complaint site (usacomplaints.com) about not being paid. The other is a litigated $217K commission dispute against an employer. These show reps being underpaid, sometimes possibly on purpose. They are not evidence that owners want, or would pay for, commission-tracking software. No owner-side quote or willingness-to-pay signal is provided.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's own demand evidence is thin: one Reddit merchant quote plus a competitor founder's origin story. Its poster-child, Zigpoll, took two years to reach traction. Zero-review apps may struggle to convert against free incumbents, and neither brief gives a listing-to-paid conversion rate. B wins mainly because A's best-sourced fact, the 5-month sales cycle, directly conflicts with the 90-day goal, not because B's demand is strongly proven."
}
```
